name: Notes to Self
description: An interactive installation where users engage in a conversation with their digital self

text: What would it feel like to sit across from yourself? Notes to Self is an interactive installation that recreates you as a digital clone and invites you to have a conversation with it.

The aim was to give people a space where they could voice their thoughts out loud without distraction. Rather than asking direct questions, the installation offers starting points, gentle openings for thoughts to trail wherever they need to go.
The project splits into three layers. The technology, the narrative, and the experience design.

Four ML models work together to mimic a person. One generates conversation, another captures and maps body movements onto a photo of the user, a third creates lip sync for the generated speech, and a fourth clones the user's voice to deliver it.
The narrative follows a classic four act structure. Exposition, complication, climax, and denouement.

Originally it included a positive turn near the end to ensure users didn't leave with heavy emotions. That safety net was removed after user research showed people preferred to sit with what they felt. They wanted to mull over the questions even after the experience ended.
The experience begins with the user sitting in front of a blank screen in a living room setting.
The screen lights up and strikes up a conversation, each sentence seemingly voiced by a different person.

'Talking to a literal screen must be unnerving,' it empathizes. Then things shift. The screen becomes a live video stream of the digital clone in a white space. The clone, now speaking in the user's voice, confirms, 'I am you, or rather a version of you.' It begins asking questions that blur the boundary between self and other. 'When was the last time we sat in silence?' 'What was the last thing our inner voice told you?'
The experience ends with the clone acknowledging that it isn't human, and that the user has helped it understand a little more about the human experience.

The user is then encouraged to stay for as long as they like. They can use the clone as a mirror, talking to themselves without prompts. A closed, judgement free space to process the conversation, or anything else on their mind. Much like a confessional.
